theme: 3 terms on numbers that get too big: the crash when a value does not fit, the operator that wraps around instead, and the protocol behind integer sizes

terms.definition: When a result is too big or too small for its integer type, so Swift stops the app with a crash.
terms.example: The badge count hit Integer Overflow because it was a `UInt8`.

terms.definition: An operator like `&+` that wraps around to the other end of the range instead of crashing.
terms.example: Use an Overflow Operator only when wrapping around is what you want.
terms.code:
let score: UInt8 = 255
let next = score &+ 1
print(next)

terms.definition: The protocol for integer types with a set number of bits, giving them `bitWidth`, `max` and overflow-checking methods.
terms.example: Make the helper generic over FixedWidthInteger, so it works for every integer size.

quizzes.question: In this code, what do you call the ampersand plus, which wraps around instead of crashing?
quizzes.code:
let score: UInt8 = 255
let next = score &+ 1 // 0

quizzes.question: Which protocol gives integer types a set number of bits, plus `bitWidth` and `max`?
What do you call it when a number grows past the biggest value its type can hold?

video.description:
Learn to explain number limits in Swift: Integer Overflow, Overflow Operator & FixedWidthInteger, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Integer Overflow - When a result is too big or too small for its integer type, so Swift stops the app with a crash.
Overflow Operator - An operator like `&+` that wraps around to the other end of the range instead of crashing.
FixedWidthInteger - The protocol for integer types with a set number of bits, giving them `bitWidth`, `max` and overflow-checking methods.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Integer Overflow, Overflow Operator & FixedWidthInteger in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
정수 오버플로, 오버플로 연산자, FixedWidthInteger 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Integer Overflow - When a result is too big or too small for its integer type, so Swift stops the app with a crash.
한국어: 정수 오버플로: 계산 결과가 정수 타입에 담기에 너무 크거나 작아서 Swift가 앱을 크래시로 멈추는 것

한국어: 오버플로 연산자: `&+`처럼 크래시 대신 범위의 반대쪽 끝으로 되감기는 연산자

한국어: FixedWidthInteger: 비트 수가 정해진 정수 타입의 프로토콜로, `bitWidth`, `max`, 오버플로 확인 메서드를 제공함

landscape.hook: Can you explain why 250 plus 10 crashed, in English?

dialogue.title: Why is it 4?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, our `hits` counter crashed at 250 plus 10. Why?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's Integer Overflow. A `UInt8` can't hold more than 255.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I switched to ampersand plus, and the crash is gone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, that's an Overflow Operator. But look, `hits` is 4 now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An Overflow Operator wraps back to zero and keeps counting. No crash, but a wrong number.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Integer Overflow is still there, just hidden?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Every FixedWidthInteger type has a fixed size and a `max`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then can I check before adding?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. `addingReportingOverflow` comes from FixedWidthInteger. It tells you if it overflowed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Or I just make `hits` an `Int` and stop worrying.

dialogue.code:
var hits: UInt8 = 250
hits = hits &+ 10
print(hits) // 4
let r = UInt8.max.addingReportingOverflow(1)
print(r.overflow) // true
